text:
Marta (sales): Acme says they need a single-page capacity plan for the commit: ~2k qps peak for chat+embeds, short unpredictable bursts. They want reserved GPU recs, autoscale policy, prewarm options, and questionnaire answers.
Diego (solutions): Do they have a traffic trace? steady vs bursty schedule matters.
Acme PM: Mostly unpredictable but concentrated around product updates. Baseline ~120 rps, bursts to ~2k for 1020m, ~610 times/month.
Ravi (eng-infra): Quick mapping: redwood-llama-8b-q ~300 qps per standard node for chat; embeddings reduce throughput so use an effective 250 qps/node mixed. That gives ~8 nodes to cover 2k. Recommend either 8 reserved for SLA or 4 reserved + autoscale.
Olga (sre): Note coldstart: model init and KV warmup can add 3-25s tail latency. For user-facing chat we should prewarm before expected launches; for unpredictable bursts consider higher reserved baseline or fast fallback.
Marta (sales): Can we provide three options with sample monthly costs and a sample autoscale policy to include in the proposal?
Ravi (eng-infra): Yes. Option 1: 8 reserved nodes (covers peak, best p99). Option 2: 4 reserved + autoscale to 12 (lower commit, some coldstart risk). Option 3: autoscale-only (no commit, highest tail latency). I'll run a perf sim and attach numbers.
Diego (solutions): Also provide a simple prewarm recipe we can run on their behalf and an SOW clause for pre-scheduled events.
Olga (sre): Prewarm snippet (short):
```
# sample autoscale & prewarm
autoscale_min: 4
autoscale_max: 12
target_rps_per_replica: 110
cooldown_sec: 60
prewarm_hook: /ops/prewarm --model=llama-8b-q --prefix-file=top_prefixes.txt --parallel=6 --duration=300
```
Prewarm CLI:
```
./prewarm --model llama-8b-q --prefix-file top_prefixes.txt --parallel 6 --duration 300
```
Olga (sre): Fallback: on repeated start failures route traffic to quantized-4bit compatible variant in-region and page on-call. Note: slight output variance may occur.
Hannah (security): Dedicated supports customer KMS and VPC peering. Audit logs default 90d; enterprise retention available as add-on. I'll answer SOC2 mapping, KMS rotation cadence, and network egress rules in the questionnaire today.
Marta (sales): Pricing examples please: show committed cost vs burst spend assuming 10 spikes/mo and 20 spikes/mo so Acme can see risk.
Ravi (eng-infra): Back-of-envelope: extra node approx $0.13/min. A 15m spike requiring +5 nodes -> 5*0.13*15 = $48.75 per spike. At 10 spikes -> ~$488/mo; at 20 -> ~$975/mo. Reserved 8-node monthly = stable commit (I'll add numbers after sim).
ci-bot: perf-sim job 1755560050 finished (status: success)
Ravi (eng-infra): Uploaded sim summary: Option 1 (8 reserved) = $BASE_A/mo, median 105ms, p99 360ms. Option 2 (4 reserved + autoscale) = $BASE_B/mo + ~$488/mo sample burst (10 spikes), median 150ms, p99 720ms. Option 3 (autoscale-only) = $BASE_C/mo, median 210ms, p99 1.7s. Full CSV in shared drive.
Marta (sales): Great. I'll draft the one-page plan with A/B/C and attach security answers. Blocking: need signed traffic trace and approval for fallback model clause and AZ spread.
Acme PM: We'll send the trace and confirm AZ spread requirement. Also want prewarm SLA for scheduled launches.
Olga (sre): We can offer a prewarm SLA for scheduled events: run prewarm 5-10m prior and confirm KV primed; ad-hoc spikes not guaranteed.
Diego (solutions): Action items: Ravi finalize pricing numbers, Olga publish prewarm runbook, Hannah finish questionnaire, Marta update SOW with fallback + AZ spread options.
Marta (sales): Thanks team 1 will send draft to Acme tomorrow.
